The bug has been fixed and verified.

### Cause of the Bug
In [`DateUtils.modify`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L619-L742), modifying time fields using `Calendar.set(...)` during Daylight Saving Time (DST) changeover (such as the fall-back transition in Mountain Time `MST7MDT`) triggered internal `Calendar` recomputations that shifted the time zone offset by an hour. In addition, setting fields when the offset was 0 caused unnecessary calendar recalculations.

### Solution
1. In [`DateUtils.modify`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L619-L742):
   - Added an immediate return when `field == Calendar.MILLISECOND`.
   - Manually truncated/rounded milliseconds, seconds, and minutes using raw millisecond offsets on `Date` before updating the calendar via `setTime(...)`.
   - Only invoked `val.set(...)` when `offset != 0`.
2. Created the focused patch file [negative_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_fix/negative_fix.patch).

### Verification
Ran `export TZ='America/Los_Angeles'; mvn test -Dtest=CucumberTest`. All 12 scenarios passed successfully with 0 failures and 0 errors.
